title: US-001 AC3 ([oracle: file-assert git check-ignore -q on each path token of the …
body: US-001 AC3 ([oracle: file-assert git check-ignore -q on each path token of the edited bullet exits non-zero]) is structurally vacuous: line 901 contains zero path tokens, so the loop body never executes and the oracle passes with zero iterations. The intent (no gitignored path token in the bullet) is satisfied, but a zero-match sweep passing silently is the same self-nullifying shape the bullet at patterns.md:901 warns about. Consider asserting a non-zero token count before iterating.

title: Worth capturing as a bullet: the review/measurement shell is zsh, where `$c:t` …
body: Worth capturing as a bullet: the review/measurement shell is zsh, where `$c:t` and `$c:s` are path modifiers, so a loop written as `git show "$c:test/foo.ts"` silently expands to `<sha>est/foo.ts` and, with stderr redirected, yields an empty file and a bogus `grep -c` of 0 for every commit. This produced two wrong measurements during this review and is the unidentified cause of the 'for-loop pipeline gave inconsistent readings' note in the round-2 artifact. Per-commit sweeps should run under an explicit `bash -c`.

title: Orphaned docstring placement: the JSDoc block describing extractCommandSubstitu…
body: Orphaned docstring placement: the JSDoc block describing extractCommandSubstitutionSpans (lines 266-280) sits immediately above findCommandSubstitutionEnd's own JSDoc block (281-288), so it visually documents the wrong function, and extractCommandSubstitutionSpans itself (line 300) has no adjacent doc comment. Move the first block down to sit directly above extractCommandSubstitutionSpans.

title: Residual (non-regression) false positive: extractCommandSubstitutionSpans splic…
body: Residual (non-regression) false positive: extractCommandSubstitutionSpans splices a preserved $(...) span back verbatim without recursively stripping quotes inside it, so inert quoted data nested in a double-quoted command substitution is still scanned. Verified: echo "$(grep -c 'x -eq 42' f)" flags on the branch. main flags it too, so this is not a regression and is out of the PRD's stated scope, but it is the same false-positive class US-001 exists to close. Consider either recursing (stripQuotedSpans on the preserved span) or extending the accepted-blind-spot bullet in patterns.md to name this shape alongside the -e case.

title: Carried over from the round-2 review and still unaddressed: the fixture-matrix …
body: Carried over from the round-2 review and still unaddressed: the fixture-matrix test uses non-null assertions (rule!.test(command!)) right after expect(...).toBeDefined(). A narrowing guard (if (!rule) throw new Error(`no such rule ${ruleName}`)) would carry the same safety without the ! escape hatch and would fail with a clearer message on a malformed fixture row.

title: The round-2 SUGGESTION about the fixture-shape guard was addressed in the data …
body: The round-2 SUGGESTION about the fixture-shape guard was addressed in the data but not in the guard: the matrix now does carry double-quoted wrapper rows and backslash-escape rows, yet the US-002 fixture-shape oracle still only counts quotedOk/grepOk/bare/wrapped, so those two new dimensions are unprotected against a future story narrowing them away. Consider extending the shape guard to require at least one double-quoted wrapper row and one backslash-escape row.
